title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one initial generation call produced per natural-language intent and that identical candidate reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial-generation calls + 1 repair call). Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition executed here. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising faster authoring of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior empirical and survey work documents LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A widely adopted architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[4]. These pipelines reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, ordering and local-policy violations), but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of such guardrails when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained task regimes.

We report a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal verifier+single-repair effect when the same initial candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). By design the experiment measures only the validator-and-repair marginal effect on identical model outputs rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. Our principal contribution is an artifact-grounded quantification of the marginal verifier-detected improvement (and its statistical bounds) under shared_initial_candidate semantics for a constrained NetOps task set.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and empirical studies establish three relevant points. First, LLMs can produce usable draft device configurations in controlled or emulation settings, though reported outputs often still require verification or correction [1],[2],[5]. Second, deterministic verification tools and formal-analysis approaches (e.g., Batfish, header-space and model-checking methods) are mature for checking reachability, forwarding, and many local-policy properties and are commonly used as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[6]. Third, generate–verify–and limited-repair workflows increase detection and correction rates for mechanically checkable defects in code and configuration domains, while deeper semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties remain difficult [4],[7].

Security analyses of prompt injection emphasize the need for filtering and validation layers in LLM-integrated pipelines; adaptive adversaries and retrieval-based attacks remain unresolved operational threats [8]. This study differs by using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect on identical candidates, by providing complete provider-call accounting and deterministic reconciliation, and by archiving validator traces and reconciliation artifacts for auditability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and specified a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, exclusion rules, analysis tests (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), and the maximum model-call budget. Preregistration SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede; the artifact is archived in the evidence bundle.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider-call accounting (explicit). Under the registered shared_initial_candidate design exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent; that identical generated candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded). Provider-call accounting reconciles model_calls_used = 251 as 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call. The adapter audit records these per-stage labels as stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} and condition_counts that reflect adapter labeling conventions: the adapter records shared initial-generation events under the "shared" label and the single repair-stage generation under the "guarded" label. This mapping is deterministic and reconciled in the deterministic_reconciliation artifact.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). Tasks exercised workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, safe access transfer patterns) and enforced protected interfaces. The full task manifest and representative payloads are archived.

Model invocation and repair policy. The declared model used for all initial generations was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). For each intent we executed one shared initial generation call. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which implements full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, counting parsed_command_count, checking required_sequence ordering, validating workflow constraints, and comparing the resulting final_state snapshot to the expected_final_state encoded in the task payload. If the validator returned valid = false for a guarded episode, the pipeline permitted up to one automated, template-driven repair (syntactic and ordering fixes only) and re-submitted the repaired candidate to the validator. No multi-iteration repairs or human escalation were permitted for confirmatory episodes.

Inclusion, contamination, and missingness rules. Exclusion rules removed items that failed vendor-parsers preventing deterministic verification or items with credential-like tokens or denylist hits. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged items were to be excluded from primary analysis. In this run no episodes were excluded or flagged; complete_pair_count = 250.

Analysis plan. The preregistered primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1. Primary test: exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; additionally a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline difference (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Secondary analyses (exploratory) include per-vendor stratifications and violation-type mixes; reported secondaries are descriptive and exploratory.
sections.results:
Execution and counts. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial-generation + 1 repair). Provider-call audit shows stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} and hosted_model_call_event_count = 251.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Deterministic validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Observed contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the one exercised repair call; the repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.4%.

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0 on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0). Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) for the guarded − baseline paired difference is [0.0, 0.012] (0–1.2 percentage points). These analysis artifacts and contingency CSVs are archived.

Representative validator diagnostics and repair. Validator traces show parsed_command_count and required_command_count equal to the task-required command counts for passed episodes (examples archived; e.g., task-000003 parsed_command_count = 6). Only one automated repair occurred and converted the sole failing baseline candidate into a guarded-pass; repair traces are archived. No episodes were excluded for contamination or parser failures.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the near‑null marginal effect. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the single permitted repair converted the only failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the possible verifier-improvement under these pipeline and task-scope choices.

Artifact-grounded reasons for the small observed gain. (1) The task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields that reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) gpt-5-mini produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents; (3) deterministic validator checks measure mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshots) and do not capture broader runtime protocol-level correctness.

Power and assumptions. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 to justify N_pairs = 250 for detecting a 15 pp effect. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed and reduces power to detect small absolute improvements; consequently the paired-bootstrap CI is the most informative practical output about the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement under the executed conditions.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity depends on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the precise validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator assesses mechanically checkable correctness but does not assert live protocol-level correctness. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; community and production-like partitions were not executed. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised. These limitations delimit the study’s generality and suggest necessary follow‑on evaluations in production-like, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair settings.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). The preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed; the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, autonomous peer-review and revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode as specified in the preregistration. Provider-call accounting reconciles model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) with stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}.

Preregistration and immutable prompt references (archived): preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution and analysis artifacts (execution manifest, raw responses, validator and repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis CSVs) are archived together in the evidence bundle referenced by the execution manifest inside the archive; full machine-verifiable manifests and per-artifact hashes are available in that bundle.

Executed estimand and scope: The confirmatory estimand executed and analyzed in this run is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition with shared_initial_candidate semantics (N_pairs = 250). The preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; any claims about sim-to-real or production-like generality are explicitly excluded by this disclosure.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
